records.source: Ἀρχὴ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: [The] beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ.
pieces: The beginning of the gospel about Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.1: [The] beginning of the gospel of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.1: This is how the good news about Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} began.

decisions.choice: a title: the opening words name what follows
alternatives: the first sentence of the story itself
decisions.reason: The line has no verb. It stands at the head of the book, or at least of its first part (1:2-13), and says where the good news begins: with John in the wilderness and Jesus' baptism.

decisions.choice: gospel: good news, the announcement of what God is doing
decisions.reason: The word means good news, used of a victory or a king's coming. Mark uses it for the message that Jesus proclaims (1:14-15). Only later did it become the name of a book.

decisions.choice: of Jesus Christ: the good news about him
alternatives: the good news that Jesus himself proclaimed
decisions.reason: Both are true in Mark, since Jesus proclaims the good news of God (1:14). Here, at the head of a story about him, Jesus is most likely the subject of the news.

decisions.choice: Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king God promised
decisions.reason: Christ is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one. Israel's kings were anointed with oil, and the prophets promised a king from David's line. In Mark it is still a title (8:29; 14:61).

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends the line at Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Many early and later manuscripts add "the Son of God", and Mark calls Jesus God's Son at key points (1:11; 15:39). A few early witnesses, including the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus, lack it. Scribes could have added the title, or dropped it by skipping a run of similar abbreviated words. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the gospel about Jesus (B); the good news about Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: "Of" could mean either, so Balanced and Readable say "about" to give the sense the meaning note prefers.

records.source: Καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν τῷ Ἠσαΐᾳ τῷ προφήτῃ· Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου·
records.gloss: As it has been written in the Isaiah the prophet, Behold, I send the messenger of me before face of you, who will prepare the way of you;
pieces: It happened just as it is written in the prophet Isaiah: "See, I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; he will make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} road ready.

L.2: Just as it has been written in Isaiah the prophet, "Look, I send {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, who will prepare {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way;

R.2: Long ago God spoke through the prophet Isaiah. He said, "Look! I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He will get the road ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: the quotation joins Exodus 23:20 and Malachi 3:1 with Isaiah 40:3 (1:3)
decisions.reason: These words come from Exodus 23:20, where God sends his messenger before Israel, and Malachi 3:1, where the messenger prepares the way before the Lord. Mark joins them to Isaiah 40:3 and names Isaiah, the prophet of the road through the wilderness, for the whole.

decisions.choice: in Isaiah the prophet, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: The oldest manuscripts name Isaiah. Many later ones read "in the prophets", most likely because scribes saw that the first lines come from elsewhere. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: just as: the scripture is fulfilled in what follows, John's coming (1:4)
alternatives: just as: the scripture backs up the title in 1:1
decisions.reason: The sentence has no main verb of its own. It most likely leads into 1:4: John came just as it was written. It could also look back to 1:1, the beginning that scripture foretold.

decisions.choice: my: God speaks; you: the one who comes, Jesus; the messenger: John
decisions.reason: In Malachi the Lord says the messenger will prepare the way "before me". Here God speaks to another, "you", whose way John prepares. Mark tells the story so that this one is Jesus (1:9).

decisions.choice: my, your, you with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: God speaks ("my") to the one whose way is prepared, Jesus ("your"), so the pronouns take the reader's capitalisation setting. "He" for the messenger is John and takes none.

decisions.choice: It happened just as (B); Long ago God spoke (R)
decisions.reason: An English sentence cannot begin with "just as" and stop. Balanced supplies "It happened", following the meaning note. Readable says that God is the speaker, as the first person "my" shows.

records.heading: The messenger in the wilderness

records.source: φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ, ἐγένετο Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ κηρύσσων βάπτισμα μετανοίας εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν.
records.gloss: [The] voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare the way of [the] Lord, straight make the paths of him, \v 4 came John the [one] baptizing in the wilderness proclaiming a baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
pieces: A voice is calling out in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord, straighten the roads {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will travel.'"
Then John the Baptizer came on the scene in the wilderness, calling people to a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of their sins.

L.3: [the] voice of one crying out in the wilderness, 'Prepare the way of [the] Lord, make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} paths straight,'"
L.4: John the Baptizer came in the wilderness, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.

R.3: Someone is shouting in the desert: 'Get the road ready for the Lord! Make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} paths straight!'"
R.4: That messenger was John the Baptizer. He came to the desert and told people to turn away from their sins and be baptized, so that God would forgive them.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 40:3: the voice that prepares the Lord's road home
decisions.reason: In Isaiah a voice calls for a road through the wilderness, so that God can lead his people home from exile. The wilderness is where John appears (1:4).

decisions.choice: the Lord: God in Isaiah; the one John prepares for is Jesus
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the Lord is God himself, the divine name. Mark sets the words so that the one whose road is made ready is Jesus, who comes in 1:9.

decisions.choice: the Baptizer: a title, the one who baptizes
alternatives: John, who was baptizing in the wilderness
decisions.reason: With the article the participle is a name for John, as in 6:14 and 6:24. Many manuscripts lack the article or add "and" before "proclaiming", which makes it a description of what John was doing.

decisions.choice: a baptism of repentance: a washing that marked a turning back to God
alternatives: a baptism that itself made people repent
decisions.reason: Repentance is a change of mind and of the whole way of life (see 1:15). Being dipped in the river showed that a person had turned back to God.

decisions.choice: for forgiveness of sins: leading to forgiveness, which God gives
alternatives: because sins had already been forgiven
decisions.reason: The word "for" points to the goal: the people who turned back would be forgiven. Forgiving sins belongs to God (2:7).

decisions.choice: the Baptizer
decisions.reason: Mark's word here is "the one who baptizes", not the noun Matthew uses (Matthew 3:1). "Baptizer" keeps the difference, which the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: That messenger was John the Baptizer.
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the quotation and the story imply, that John is the messenger and the voice of 1:2-3.

records.source: καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία χώρα καὶ οἱ Ἱεροσολυμῖται πάντες, καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And were going out to him all the Judean region and the Jerusalemites all, and were being baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing the sins of them.
pieces: The whole land of Judea and everyone from Jerusalem kept going out to him. They confessed their sins, and he baptized them in the Jordan River.

L.5: And all the Judean region and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him, and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.

R.5: People came to him from everywhere in Judea and from the city of Jerusalem. They told God the wrong things they had done, and John baptized them in the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: all: a great many, the whole region in motion
decisions.reason: "All" stresses how many came, as people speak of a whole town turning out. Mark later says that the leaders did not accept John (11:30-31).

decisions.choice: were going out, were being baptized: a stream of people over time
alternatives: a single crowd on one day
decisions.reason: The verbs are continuous: people kept coming and being baptized.

decisions.choice: confessing: openly admitting their sins
decisions.reason: The word means to agree openly, to say out loud. Here it is the sins that are owned up to.

decisions.choice: the Jordan River: the river running from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea
alternatives: a pool or stream near Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Jordan was the border Israel crossed to enter the promised land (Joshua 3). John baptized in the wilderness stretch near Jericho.

decisions.choice: told God the wrong things they had done
decisions.reason: Readable says what confessing sins means in plain words. Confession was made before God, and the crowd heard it.

records.source: καὶ ἦν ὁ Ἰωάννης ἐνδεδυμένος τρίχας καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσθων ἀκρίδας καὶ μέλι ἄγριον.
records.gloss: And was the John clothed [in] hair of camel and a belt leathern around the waist of him, and eating locusts and honey wild.
pieces: John's clothes were made of camel's hair, and he had a leather belt around his waist. He lived on locusts and wild honey.

L.6: And John was clothed [in] camel's hair and [had] a leather belt around his waist, and [he was] eating locusts and wild honey.

R.6: John wore clothes made from camel hair, with a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts, a kind of grasshopper, and honey that he found in the wild.

decisions.choice: camel's hair and a leather belt: the dress of Elijah
alternatives: simply the clothing of a poor man
decisions.reason: Elijah is described as a hairy man with a leather belt around his waist (2 Kings 1:8). Malachi 4:5 promised that Elijah would come before the day of the Lord, and Jesus later says that he has come (9:13).

decisions.choice: locusts and wild honey: food found in the wilderness
alternatives: a special diet for a vow
decisions.reason: Locusts were clean food under the law (Leviticus 11:22), and wild bees' honey could be found in rocks and trees. John lived on what the wilderness gave.

decisions.choice: locusts, a kind of grasshopper
decisions.reason: Many readers do not know that a locust is an insect, so Readable says so, as in Matthew 3:4.

records.source: καὶ ἐκήρυσσεν λέγων· Ἔρχεται ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου ὀπίσω μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς κύψας λῦσαι τὸν ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: And he was proclaiming saying, Comes the [one] mightier [than] me after me, of whom not I am worthy having stooped down to untie the strap of the sandals of him.
pieces: This was his message: "Someone stronger than I am is coming after me. I am not fit even to bend down and untie the strap of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals.

L.7: And he was proclaiming, saying, "One mightier than I is coming after me; I am not fit to stoop down [and] untie the strap of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals.

R.7: He told the people, "Someone much greater than I am is coming after me. I am not good enough even to bend down and untie {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals.

decisions.choice: the one coming after me: the Messiah, whom John does not name
decisions.reason: John points away from himself to one greater, who will baptize with the Holy Spirit (1:8). Mark's next scene shows who it is (1:9-11).

decisions.choice: untie his sandals: the task of the lowest slave
decisions.reason: Taking off a master's sandals was a slave's job. John says he is not fit to do even that for the one who is coming.

decisions.choice: after me: later in time
decisions.reason: The words can mean "behind", as a disciple follows a teacher, but here they mean that the mightier one comes after John's work.

decisions.choice: not fit
decisions.reason: The word means sufficient or fit for a task, and Matthew 3:11 uses "fit" for the same saying.

records.source: ἐγὼ ἐβάπτισα ὑμᾶς ὕδατι, αὐτὸς δὲ βαπτίσει ὑμᾶς ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.
records.gloss: I baptized you with water, he but will baptize you in [the] Spirit Holy.
pieces: The baptism I gave you was with water; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."

L.8: I baptized you with water, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will baptize you in [the] Holy Spirit."

R.8: I used water when I baptized you. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."

decisions.choice: I baptized: John looks at the work he has done
decisions.reason: The verb is past. John speaks of his baptism as done, set against what the coming one will do.

decisions.choice: baptize with the Holy Spirit: pour out God's Spirit on people
decisions.reason: The prophets promised that God would pour out his Spirit on his people (Joel 2:28; Ezekiel 36:26-27). The one who is coming will do what water only pictures.

decisions.choice: in the Spirit: the Spirit is what people will be plunged into
alternatives: by the Spirit, as the one who acts
decisions.reason: Water and the Spirit stand side by side as the element of each baptism.

decisions.choice: with water, in the Holy Spirit (L); with ... with (B, R)
alternatives: in water, in the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: The Greek has no preposition with "water" and "in" with "Spirit". Literal keeps the difference. Balanced and Readable say "with" for both, the natural English.

records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲτ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη εἰς τὸν Ἰορδάνην ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου.
records.gloss: And it came to pass in those the days came Jesus from Nazareth of the Galilee and was baptized into the Jordan by John.
pieces: It was during those days that Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee, and John baptized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the Jordan.

L.9: And it happened in those days [that] Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized into the Jordan by John.

R.9: During that time, Jesus came from the town of Nazareth in the land of Galilee. John baptized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: it happened: the old biblical way of starting a new event
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the style of the Greek Old Testament and simply opens a new scene.

decisions.choice: Nazareth of Galilee: a small village in the hills of Galilee
decisions.reason: Nazareth is not named in the Old Testament and was an unimportant place (John 1:46). Galilee was the northern region, far from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: into the Jordan: Jesus went down into the river
alternatives: at the Jordan, on the bank
decisions.reason: "Into" pictures him being dipped in the water. He comes up out of it in 1:10.

decisions.choice: it happened (L only); John baptized him (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out the old opening phrase and make John the subject, which reads more naturally.

records.heading: Jesus is baptized

records.source: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀναβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος εἶδεν σχιζομένους τοὺς οὐρανοὺς καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα ὡς περιστερὰν καταβαῖνον εἰς αὐτόν·
records.gloss: And immediately going up out of the water he saw being torn open the heavens and the Spirit as a dove coming down into him.
pieces: The moment {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came up out of the water, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit coming down on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} like a dove.

L.10: And immediately, coming up out of the water, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit like a dove coming down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.10: Right away, as Jesus was coming up out of the water, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw heaven torn open. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the Spirit coming down on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} like a dove.

decisions.choice: immediately: Mark's word for moving the story straight on
decisions.reason: Mark uses this word more than forty times, eleven in this chapter. Often it means "at once"; sometimes it just carries the reader into the next event.

decisions.choice: torn open: a violent tearing, not a gentle opening
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when the temple curtain is torn from top to bottom at Jesus' death (15:38). Isaiah 64:1 asks God to tear open the heavens and come down.

decisions.choice: he saw: Jesus is the one who sees
decisions.reason: The subject is still Jesus, who is coming up out of the water, and the voice in 1:11 speaks to him.

decisions.choice: like a dove: the Spirit's coming down is compared to a dove
alternatives: the Spirit took the bodily form of a dove
decisions.reason: The words can describe the way the Spirit came down or what was seen. Luke 3:22 says it was in bodily form; Mark only gives the comparison.

decisions.choice: to him: the Spirit came down upon him
decisions.reason: The word can mean "into", but after a verb of coming down it is often "to" or "upon", as in Matthew 3:16.

decisions.choice: immediately (L); the moment (B); right away (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word for this Greek word throughout. Balanced and Readable vary it, so that Mark's quick pace does not become a repeated word in English.

records.source: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν· Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν σοὶ εὐδόκησα.
records.gloss: And a voice came out of the heavens, You are the Son of me the beloved, in you I was well pleased.
pieces: Then a voice spoke from heaven: "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dearly loved Son. I take delight in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

L.11: And a voice came out of the heavens: "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, the beloved; in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I am well pleased."

R.11: Then a voice from heaven said, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, and I love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I am very pleased with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: you are my Son ... I am well pleased: Psalm 2:7 and Isaiah 42:1
decisions.reason: In Psalm 2:7 God says to his anointed king, "You are my son". In Isaiah 42:1 God delights in his chosen servant and puts his Spirit on him. "Beloved son" also recalls Isaac (Genesis 22:2).

decisions.choice: I am well pleased: a settled delight
alternatives: God became pleased at the baptism
decisions.reason: The past tense here states God's approval as a fact, not a change that has just happened.

decisions.choice: You are: the voice speaks to Jesus himself
alternatives: the voice speaks about him to the crowd
decisions.reason: In Mark the voice says "you". Matthew 3:17 has "This is", addressed to those present.

decisions.choice: Son with a capital letter
decisions.reason: The word is a title here, as in 1:1 and 15:39, so it is capitalized, as at Matthew 3:17.

records.source: Καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτὸν ἐκβάλλει εἰς τὴν ἔρημον.
records.gloss: And immediately the Spirit him drives out into the wilderness.
pieces: Straight away the Spirit drove {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out into the wilderness.

L.12: And immediately the Spirit drives {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out into the wilderness.

R.12: Right after that, the Spirit pushed Jesus to go out into the desert.

decisions.choice: drives out: sends with force
decisions.reason: This is the verb used for casting out demons (1:34, 39). It shows urgency and the Spirit's power, not hostility. Matthew 4:1 and Luke 4:1 say "led".

decisions.choice: drives: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: where Israel was tested
decisions.reason: Israel was led through the wilderness for forty years and tested there (Deuteronomy 8:2).

decisions.choice: drives (L); drove (B); pushed ... to go (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Mark's present tense. Balanced and Readable use the past, as English tells a story.

records.heading: Forty days in the wilderness

records.source: καὶ ἦν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τεσσεράκοντα ἡμέρας πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ ἦν μετὰ τῶν θηρίων, καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And he was in the wilderness forty days being tempted by the Satan, and was with the wild beasts, and the angels were serving him.
pieces: He stayed in the wilderness for forty days while Satan tempted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He was among the wild animals, and the angels took care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.13: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in the wilderness forty days, being tempted by Satan, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was with the wild animals, and the angels were serving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.13: Jesus was in the desert for forty days, and Satan tried to make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do wrong. Wild animals were there with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and angels took care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: tempted: put to the test, here by one who wants him to fail
alternatives: only tested to show his strength
decisions.reason: The word covers both testing and temptation. Satan's aim is to make Jesus turn from God's way.

decisions.choice: Satan: the adversary, the enemy of God
decisions.reason: The name means accuser or adversary. Matthew and Luke call him the devil in this story.

decisions.choice: forty days: Israel's forty years, and the forty days of Moses and Elijah
decisions.reason: Israel was tested for forty years in the wilderness. Moses was on the mountain forty days (Exodus 34:28), and Elijah walked forty days to Horeb (1 Kings 19:8).

decisions.choice: with the wild animals: in dangerous, empty country
alternatives: at peace with the animals, as in Isaiah 11:6-9
decisions.reason: Mark does not say what the animals mean. They show how wild the place was; some read them as a sign of the peace of God's new age.

decisions.choice: were serving him: caring for his needs
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Simon's mother-in-law in 1:31. Angels brought Elijah food in the wilderness (1 Kings 19:5-7).

decisions.choice: tried to make him do wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what tempting means in plain words, as in Matthew 4:1.

records.source: Καὶ μετὰ τὸ παραδοθῆναι τὸν Ἰωάννην ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ λέγων ὅτι Πεπλήρωται ὁ καιρὸς καὶ ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ· μετανοεῖτε καὶ πιστεύετε ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.
records.gloss: And after the to be handed over the John came the Jesus into the Galilee proclaiming the gospel of the God \v 15 and saying, Has been fulfilled the time and has come near the kingdom of the God; repent and believe in the gospel.
pieces: After John had been handed over, Jesus went into Galilee, proclaiming God's gospel.
"The appointed time has arrived in full," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "and the kingdom of God has come near. Repent, and believe in the gospel."

L.14: And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the gospel of God
L.15: and saying, "The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent and believe in the gospel."

R.14: After John was put in prison, Jesus went to Galilee and told people the good news from God.
R.15: He said, "The time God promised has come. The kingdom of God is coming near. Turn away from your sins and come back to God, and believe the good news!"

decisions.choice: handed over: arrested and put in prison
decisions.reason: Mark tells of John's arrest in 6:17. The same verb is used of Jesus being handed over (9:31; 14:41) and then of his followers (13:9), so John's path foreshadows theirs.

decisions.choice: the gospel of God: the good news that comes from God
decisions.reason: God is the source of the news. Its content is what Jesus says next: God's kingdom has come near.

decisions.choice: the time has been fulfilled: the time God set has fully come
alternatives: time in general has run out
decisions.reason: The word for time is the appointed moment. What the prophets waited for has arrived.

decisions.choice: has come near: it is close at hand, already pressing in
decisions.reason: The perfect tense says the kingdom has drawn near and is now close. Matthew 4:17 has the same verb. God's rule is breaking in through Jesus' words and works.

decisions.choice: believe in the gospel: trust the message and rely on it
decisions.reason: Believing "in" a message is an unusual phrase. It means putting one's trust in the news that God's kingdom has come near.

decisions.choice: was put in prison
decisions.reason: Readable says what being handed over meant for John, which Mark tells in 6:17.

decisions.choice: turn away from your sins and come back to God
decisions.reason: Readable says what repenting means, as in Matthew 3:2 and 4:17.

records.heading: The kingdom of God has come near

records.source: Καὶ παράγων παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν Σίμωνα καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν Σίμωνος ἀμφιβάλλοντας ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλιεῖς·
records.gloss: And passing by beside the sea of the Galilee he saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting in the sea; they were for fishermen.
pieces: As Jesus went along the shore of the Sea of Galilee, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw Simon and Simon's brother Andrew throwing a net into the water. They fished for a living.

L.16: And passing along beside the Sea of Galilee, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw Simon and Andrew, Simon's brother, casting [a net] in the sea, for they were fishermen.

R.16: One day Jesus was walking beside Lake Galilee. He saw Simon and his brother Andrew throwing a net into the lake to catch fish, because they were fishermen.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Galilee: a freshwater lake about thirteen miles long
decisions.reason: The Greek calls it a sea, following Hebrew usage, but it is a large lake. Fishing was one of the main trades of the towns on its shore.

decisions.choice: casting: throwing a round net by hand
decisions.reason: The verb itself means throwing around; it was used for a casting net, thrown from the shore or from shallow water.

decisions.choice: a net (L in brackets, B, R); Jesus (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "casting". Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the last sentence spoke of him only by "he".

decisions.choice: Lake Galilee
decisions.reason: Readable calls it a lake, which is what it is, as in Matthew 4:18.

records.heading: Four fishermen follow Jesus

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου, καὶ ποιήσω ὑμᾶς γενέσθαι ἁλιεῖς ἀνθρώπων.
records.gloss: And said to them the Jesus, Come after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
pieces: Jesus said to them, "Come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will make you into fishers of {{gender:people|men}}."

L.17: And Jesus said to them, "Come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will make you become fishers of {{gender:people|men}}."

R.17: Jesus said to them, "Come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will teach you to catch {{gender:people|men}} instead of fish."

decisions.choice: come after me: become my disciples, following me as your teacher
alternatives: walk behind me for a while
decisions.reason: Disciples walked behind their teacher, learning from him as they went.

decisions.choice: fishers of people: they will gather people for God's kingdom
alternatives: a threat of judgment, as fishing is in Jeremiah 16:16
decisions.reason: Jesus takes their trade as a picture of their new work, bringing people in to God's kingdom.

decisions.choice: men: human beings
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for human beings, so the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: I will make you become: they will grow into this work
alternatives: they are fishers of people at once
decisions.reason: Mark has "become", which Matthew 4:19 does not. The change takes time, and the disciples are sent out in 6:7.

records.source: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀφέντες τὰ δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And immediately having left the nets they followed him.
pieces: They dropped their nets on the spot and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.18: And immediately, leaving the nets, they followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.18: Right away they left their nets and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: followed him: went with him as his disciples
alternatives: walked behind him for a short time
decisions.reason: To follow a teacher was to become his disciple and share his life.

decisions.choice: immediately ... leaving: a response with no delay or conditions
decisions.reason: They leave their nets, their living, at once (see 10:28).

records.source: καὶ προβὰς ὀλίγον εἶδεν Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ καταρτίζοντας τὰ δίκτυα, καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκάλεσεν αὐτούς.
records.gloss: And having gone on a little he saw James the [son] of the Zebedee and John the brother of him, and them in the boat mending the nets, \v 20 and immediately he called them.
pieces: He went on a little way and saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John, who were in their boat putting their nets in order.
He called them at once.

L.19: And going on a little, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw James the [son] of Zebedee and John his brother, and they [were] in the boat mending the nets,

R.19: Jesus walked on a little farther and saw James and John, the sons of Zebedee. They were in their boat, fixing their fishing nets.
R.20: Right away Jesus called them to come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: mending: repairing or getting the nets ready
decisions.reason: The word means to put in order: to mend what is torn or to make the nets ready for use.

decisions.choice: the [son] of Zebedee: the article stands for "son"
decisions.reason: Greek often names a man by his father with the article alone. Zebedee is their father (1:20).

decisions.choice: called them: summoned them to be his disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus calls them as he called Simon and Andrew (1:17), and they follow (1:20).

decisions.choice: called them to come with him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the call was for, as in Matthew 4:21.

records.source: καὶ ἀφέντες τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν Ζεβεδαῖον ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ μετὰ τῶν μισθωτῶν ἀπῆλθον ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: and having left the father of them Zebedee in the boat with the hired men they went away after him.
pieces: Leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers, they went off after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.20: And leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men, they went away after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.20: They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the workers he paid, and they went with Jesus.

decisions.choice: the hired men: Zebedee's paid workers
decisions.reason: Zebedee's fishing business had hired workers, so the sons did not leave their father alone, but they did leave a family business.

decisions.choice: went away after him: left to become his followers
alternatives: went on a short trip with him
decisions.reason: "After him" echoes "come after me" (1:17).

decisions.choice: went with Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what following meant, and names Jesus.

records.source: Καὶ εἰσπορεύονται εἰς Καφαρναούμ.
records.gloss: And they go into Capernaum.
pieces: They made their way to Capernaum.

R.21: Then they went to the town of Capernaum.

decisions.choice: Capernaum: a fishing town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Capernaum became the base of Jesus' work in Galilee (2:1).

decisions.choice: they go: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid.

decisions.choice: go (L); made their way (B); went (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Mark's present tense. Balanced and Readable use the past.

records.heading: A new teaching, with authority

records.source: καὶ εὐθὺς τοῖς σάββασιν ἐδίδασκεν εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν.
records.gloss: and immediately on the Sabbaths he was teaching into the synagogue.
pieces: On the Sabbath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went straight into the synagogue and taught there.

L.21: And immediately on the Sabbath, [going] into the synagogue, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching.

R.21: On the Sabbath, the weekly day of rest, Jesus went into the synagogue, where the Jews met to worship, and taught the people.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbaths: on the Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The plural is the normal way of naming the Sabbath day, like the Hebrew. One day is meant, as the story that follows shows.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verb for entering
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "having gone into the synagogue, he was teaching". The SBLGNT text has only "into the synagogue", which still implies that he went in. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the synagogue: the meeting place for prayer and reading the law
decisions.reason: Jews met in the synagogue on the Sabbath to pray and to hear the scriptures read and explained. A visiting teacher could be asked to speak.

decisions.choice: he was teaching: he taught, and kept on teaching
alternatives: he had been teaching for a long time
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous, setting the scene for what happened while he taught (1:23).

decisions.choice: the weekly day of rest; where the Jews met to worship
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two words for readers who do not know them.

records.source: καὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ, ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς.
records.gloss: And they were astonished at the teaching of him; he was for teaching them as authority having and not as the scribes.
pieces: His teaching astounded them. Unlike the scribes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them as someone who has authority.

L.22: And they were astonished at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching them as [one] having authority, and not as the scribes.

R.22: The people were amazed at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching. He did not teach like the teachers of God's law. He taught like someone who had real authority.

decisions.choice: astonished: struck with amazement
decisions.reason: The word means to be overwhelmed by something. It says nothing yet about whether they believed.

decisions.choice: authority: the right and the power to speak and act
decisions.reason: Jesus' authority is shown at once over an unclean spirit (1:27). His opponents later ask where his authority comes from (11:28).

decisions.choice: the scribes: experts in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The scribes taught the law and how to keep it, often by quoting earlier teachers. They become Jesus' opponents (2:6; 3:22).

decisions.choice: the teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: Readable uses a name that says what the scribes did, as in Matthew 2:4.

records.source: καὶ εὐθὺς ἦν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ καὶ ἀνέκραξεν λέγων· Τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Ναζαρηνέ;
records.gloss: And immediately there was in the synagogue of them a man in a spirit unclean, and he cried out \v 24 saying, What to us and to you, Jesus Nazarene?
pieces: Right then, in their synagogue, there was a man with an unclean spirit, and he screamed,
"What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth?

L.23: And immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
L.24: saying, "What [is there] to us and to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Jesus of Nazareth?

R.23: Right then a man with an evil spirit in him was in the synagogue. He shouted,
R.24: "Jesus from Nazareth, why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bothering us?

decisions.choice: with an unclean spirit: in the power of an unclean spirit
alternatives: a man who had a bad attitude
decisions.reason: "In a spirit" means held under the spirit's power. The spirit speaks through the man.

decisions.choice: an unclean spirit: an evil spirit, a demon
decisions.reason: Mark calls these beings both unclean spirits and demons (1:34; 3:22, 30). "Unclean" sets them against the Holy Spirit (1:8) and the Holy One of God (1:24).

decisions.choice: what to us and to you: what do we have in common? leave us alone
alternatives: what do you want from us, a friendly question
decisions.reason: The phrase keeps someone at a distance (Judges 11:12; 1 Kings 17:18). Here it is hostile.

decisions.choice: us: the spirit speaks for all the unclean spirits
alternatives: the man and the spirit together
decisions.reason: The spirit speaks for its kind, which Jesus has come to defeat (3:27).

decisions.choice: an evil spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says "evil", since "unclean" suggests dirt to new readers.

records.source: ἦλθες ἀπολέσαι ἡμᾶς;
records.gloss: Did you come to destroy us?
pieces: Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} here to destroy us?

R.24: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come to get rid of us?

decisions.choice: a question, as the SBLGNT prints it
alternatives: a statement: You have come to destroy us!
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have no question marks, and the words can be read either way. The question fits the alarm of the other questions around it.

decisions.choice: destroy: the end of the evil spirits' power
decisions.reason: The spirit fears the judgment that God's kingdom brings on evil.

records.source: οἶδά σε τίς εἶ, ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: I know you who you are, the holy [one] of the God.
pieces: I know who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are: God's Holy One!"

L.24: I know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are: the Holy One of God."

R.24: I know who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. You are God's Holy One!"

decisions.choice: the Holy One of God: the one set apart and belonging to God
decisions.reason: The spirit, unclean, names Jesus as the one who is holy, belonging wholly to God (compare John 6:69).

decisions.choice: I know who you are: naming him to resist him
decisions.reason: Knowing and saying another's name was thought to give power over him. Jesus silences the spirit (1:25).

records.source: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Φιμώθητι καὶ ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And rebuked him the Jesus saying, Be silenced and come out of him.
pieces: Jesus ordered it sternly, "Silence! Come out of the man!"

L.25: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, "Be silenced, and come out of him!"

R.25: Jesus spoke strongly to the evil spirit. He said, "Be quiet! Come out of the man!"

decisions.choice: rebuked: gave a stern command
decisions.reason: The word is used for Jesus' commands to spirits (3:12) and to the wind and sea (4:39). It is a word of power.

decisions.choice: be silenced: be muzzled, stop speaking
decisions.reason: The verb means to muzzle. Jesus will not let the spirit name him (1:34).

decisions.choice: him: the spirit is addressed; the man is the one it leaves
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the spirit and orders it out of the man.

decisions.choice: it; the man (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "it" for the spirit and "the man" for the one it is in, so that the two are not confused.

records.source: καὶ σπαράξαν αὐτὸν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον καὶ φωνῆσαν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐξῆλθεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And having convulsed him the spirit the unclean and having cried with a voice loud it came out of him.
pieces: The unclean spirit threw the man into a fit, gave a loud shriek, and left him.

L.26: And the unclean spirit, throwing him into convulsions and crying out with a loud voice, came out of him.

R.26: The evil spirit made the man shake hard. Then it gave a loud scream and came out of him.

decisions.choice: throwing into convulsions: shaking him violently
decisions.reason: The word describes a violent fit (9:26). The man is not harmed in the end.

decisions.choice: crying out: the spirit's last protest as it obeys
decisions.reason: The spirit cries out but has to leave, which the crowd notices (1:27).

records.source: καὶ ἐθαμβήθησαν ἅπαντες, ὥστε συζητεῖν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντας· Τί ἐστιν τοῦτο;
records.gloss: And were amazed all, so that to discuss with themselves saying, What is this?
pieces: Amazement seized them all, and they talked it over among themselves: "What is this?

L.27: And they were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, "What is this?

R.27: All the people were amazed. They asked each other, "What is happening?

decisions.choice: amazed: astonished, close to alarm
decisions.reason: The word is stronger than the one in 1:22 and has a sense of awe and fear.

decisions.choice: questioned among themselves: discussed and argued
decisions.reason: They talk it over with each other, trying to understand what they saw.

records.source: διδαχὴ καινή· κατ’ ἐξουσίαν καὶ τοῖς πνεύμασι τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις ἐπιτάσσει, καὶ ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: A teaching new with authority; even the spirits the unclean he commands, and they obey him.
pieces: A new kind of teaching, backed by authority! At {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} command even the unclean spirits do as they are told."

L.27: A new teaching with authority! Even the unclean spirits {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commands, and they obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.27: This man teaches something new, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} teaches with authority! He even tells evil spirits what to do, and they obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

decisions.choice: with authority goes with the new teaching
alternatives: with authority he commands even the unclean spirits
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a break after "with authority", so the phrase describes the teaching. With the break before it, it describes the commands. Either way Jesus' word has authority.

decisions.choice: new: new in kind, not only recent
decisions.reason: The word means fresh or of a new kind. Teaching that drives out spirits by a word is something the people have not met before.

decisions.choice: even unclean spirits obey him: his word has God's power
decisions.reason: Jesus uses no ritual or name, only a command, and the spirits must obey.

records.source: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἡ ἀκοὴ αὐτοῦ εὐθὺς πανταχοῦ εἰς ὅλην τὴν περίχωρον τῆς Γαλιλαίας.
records.gloss: And went out the report of him immediately everywhere into all the surrounding region of the Galilee.
pieces: The news about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} went out at once in every direction, through all the country around Galilee.

L.28: And the report about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} went out immediately everywhere, into the whole surrounding region of Galilee.

R.28: Very quickly, people all over the area of Galilee heard about Jesus.

decisions.choice: the surrounding region of Galilee: the whole region of Galilee round about
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means all of Galilee around Capernaum, though it could include lands beyond it.

decisions.choice: report: what people heard and told about him
decisions.reason: The word means something heard, news passed on by word of mouth.

records.source: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς ἐξελθόντες ἦλθον εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Σίμωνος καὶ Ἀνδρέου μετὰ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωάννου.
records.gloss: And immediately out of the synagogue having gone out they came into the house of Simon and Andrew with James and John.
pieces: They left the synagogue and went straight to the house where Simon and Andrew lived, and James and John came with them.

L.29: And immediately, going out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.

R.29: Right after that, they left the synagogue and went to Simon and Andrew's house. James and John went with them.

decisions.choice: they went out and came: the plural, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have the singular, with Jesus as the subject. With the plural, "they" are Jesus and the four disciples. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the house of Simon and Andrew: the brothers' home in Capernaum
alternatives: a house they rented for Jesus
decisions.reason: John 1:44 says the brothers came from Bethsaida; by now they lived in Capernaum, where Simon's family was.

records.heading: Simon's mother-in-law

records.source: ἡ δὲ πενθερὰ Σίμωνος κατέκειτο πυρέσσουσα, καὶ εὐθὺς λέγουσιν αὐτῷ περὶ αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: And the mother-in-law of Simon was lying down fevering, and immediately they speak to him about her.
pieces: Simon's mother-in-law lay ill with a fever, and they lost no time in telling {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about her.

L.30: Now Simon's mother-in-law was lying down sick with a fever, and immediately they tell {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about her.

R.30: Simon's mother-in-law was lying in bed with a fever. Right away they told Jesus that she was sick.

decisions.choice: Simon's mother-in-law: Simon was married
decisions.reason: Paul says that Peter took his wife with him on his travels (1 Corinthians 9:5).

decisions.choice: lying down with a fever: too ill to get up
decisions.reason: Fever could be a sign of serious illness, and she was in bed with it.

decisions.choice: they speak: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark tells this in the present tense to make it vivid.

records.source: καὶ προσελθὼν ἤγειρεν αὐτὴν κρατήσας τῆς χειρός· καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτὴν ὁ πυρετός, καὶ διηκόνει αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: And having come to [her] he raised her having taken hold of the hand; and left her the fever, and she was serving them.
pieces: He came over, took hold of her hand, and lifted her up. Her fever was gone, and she started to look after them.

L.31: And coming to [her], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised her up, taking hold of [her] hand; and the fever left her, and she began serving them.

R.31: Jesus went to her. He took her hand and helped her get up. The fever went away, and she began to serve them food.

decisions.choice: raised her up: helped her to stand
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for raising the dead (5:41; 16:6), but here it means getting her up from her bed.

decisions.choice: serving them: looking after them as her guests
decisions.reason: She took up the work of a host, which shows that the cure was complete. The same verb is used of the angels in 1:13 and of Jesus himself in 10:45.

decisions.choice: she began serving: the imperfect describes what she went on doing
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous: she got up and set about caring for them.

decisions.choice: serve them food
decisions.reason: Readable says what serving guests most likely meant here: giving them a meal.

records.source: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης, ὅτε ἔδυ ὁ ἥλιος, ἔφερον πρὸς αὐτὸν πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας καὶ τοὺς δαιμονιζομένους·
records.gloss: Evening and having come, when set the sun, they were bringing to him all the [ones] badly having and the [ones] being demon-possessed.
pieces: When evening came and the sun had set, people began bringing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} everyone who was ill or controlled by demons.

L.32: Now when evening had come, when the sun set, they were bringing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all who were sick and those who were demon-possessed.

R.32: That evening, after the sun went down, people brought all the sick to Jesus, and all who had demons in them.

decisions.choice: when the sun set: the Sabbath ended at sunset
decisions.reason: The Sabbath of 1:21 ended at sunset. Then people could carry the sick without breaking the Sabbath rest.

decisions.choice: demon-possessed: under the control of demons
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the sick and the demon-possessed apart (1:34): illness is healed, demons are cast out.

decisions.choice: they were bringing: one after another
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous: people kept bringing the sick.

records.heading: The whole town at the door

records.source: καὶ ἦν ὅλη ἡ πόλις ἐπισυνηγμένη πρὸς τὴν θύραν.
records.gloss: And was all the city gathered together at the door.
pieces: The entire town had crowded together outside the door.

L.33: And the whole city was gathered together at the door.

R.33: Almost everyone in the town crowded around the door of the house.

decisions.choice: the whole city: a great crowd from the town
decisions.reason: "Whole" stresses how many came, as in 1:5.

decisions.choice: city: a town
decisions.reason: The word is used for any town with walls or a council. Capernaum was a lakeside town.

decisions.choice: town (B, R); city (L)
decisions.reason: Capernaum was small, so Balanced and Readable say "town". Readable says "almost everyone" to show the exaggeration.

records.source: καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ποικίλαις νόσοις, καὶ δαιμόνια πολλὰ ἐξέβαλεν, καὶ οὐκ ἤφιεν λαλεῖν τὰ δαιμόνια, ὅτι ᾔδεισαν αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And he healed many badly having various diseases and demons many he cast out, and not he was allowing to speak the demons, because they knew him.
pieces: He cured many people who had diseases of every kind, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} threw out many demons. He did not permit the demons to say anything, since they knew {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.34: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed many who were sick with various diseases, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cast out many demons; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not allowing the demons to speak, because they knew {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.34: Jesus healed many people who had all kinds of sicknesses. He forced many demons to leave people. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not let the demons talk, because they knew who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was.

decisions.choice: many: a great number, not a hint that some were left unhealed
decisions.reason: In Hebrew and Greek, "many" can stand for a large whole, as in 10:45. Matthew 8:16 says he healed all who were sick.

decisions.choice: he would not let the demons speak: he kept them from making him known
alternatives: he did not want to hear lies
decisions.reason: The demons knew who he was (1:24). Jesus silences them, as he does in 3:11-12, and makes himself known in his own way and time.

decisions.choice: they knew him, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "to be the Christ", likely from Luke 4:41. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: cast out: drove out with force
decisions.reason: This is the verb of 1:12, used for expelling demons by command.

decisions.choice: threw out (B); forced ... to leave (R)
decisions.reason: "Cast out" is old church language. Balanced uses an everyday verb with the same force.

records.source: Καὶ πρωῒ ἔννυχα λίαν ἀναστὰς ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κἀκεῖ προσηύχετο.
records.gloss: And early in night very having risen he went out and went away into a solitary place, and there he was praying.
pieces: Long before daylight, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got up and went out. He went off to a lonely place and spent time there in prayer.

L.35: And very early, while still night, rising up, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out and went away into a deserted place, and there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was praying.

R.35: Very early the next morning, before it got light, Jesus got up and left the house. He went to a place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could be alone, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prayed there.

decisions.choice: very early, while still night: before dawn
decisions.reason: The three words together mean the last part of the night, before first light.

decisions.choice: a deserted place: the word for the wilderness of 1:3-13
decisions.reason: The place is "wilderness-like", empty of people. Jesus withdraws there to pray, as he will again (6:46; 14:32-39).

decisions.choice: he was praying: he spent time in prayer
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous; he was still praying when they found him (1:37).

decisions.choice: left the house
decisions.reason: Readable says where he went out from, Simon's house (1:29).

records.heading: On to the nearby towns

records.source: καὶ κατεδίωξεν αὐτὸν Σίμων καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εὗρον αὐτὸν καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ ὅτι Πάντες ζητοῦσίν σε.
records.gloss: And hunted down him Simon and those with him, \v 37 and found him and they say to him, All are seeking you.
pieces: Simon and the others with him tracked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down.
Finding {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they said, "Everybody is out looking for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

L.36: And Simon and those with him searched hard for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
L.37: and they found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Everyone is looking for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.36: Simon and his friends went to look for Jesus.
R.37: They found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "All the people are looking for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

decisions.choice: searched hard for: hunted him down
decisions.reason: The verb means to pursue closely. They are eager to bring him back to the crowds.

decisions.choice: those with him: Andrew, James and John
decisions.reason: These are the others who were with Simon in 1:29.

decisions.choice: they say: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark tells this in the present tense to make it vivid.

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἄγωμεν ἀλλαχοῦ εἰς τὰς ἐχομένας κωμοπόλεις, ἵνα καὶ ἐκεῖ κηρύξω, εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ἐξῆλθον.
records.gloss: And he says to them, Let us go elsewhere into the neighboring towns, so that also there I may proclaim; for this for I came out.
pieces: He replied, "Let us move on to the market towns nearby, so that I can proclaim the message there as well. This is what I came out to do."

L.38: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Let us go elsewhere, into the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim there also; for this is why I came out."

R.38: Jesus said to them, "Let us go to the other towns near here, so that I can tell people the good news there too. That is why I came."

decisions.choice: towns: market towns, larger than villages
decisions.reason: The word joins village and city: country towns with their own markets.

decisions.choice: I came out: from Capernaum, or from God who sent him
alternatives: I came out of the house this morning
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean that this is why he left the town, to preach elsewhere. Luke 4:43 says "I was sent", and the words may also hint at his mission from God.

decisions.choice: so that I may proclaim: his purpose is to preach, not only to heal
alternatives: so that I can heal there
decisions.reason: He leaves the crowd that came for healing and goes to proclaim the kingdom (1:14-15).

decisions.choice: tell people the good news
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus proclaimed, the good news of 1:14-15.

records.source: καὶ ἦλθεν κηρύσσων εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς αὐτῶν εἰς ὅλην τὴν Γαλιλαίαν καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλων.
records.gloss: And he came proclaiming into the synagogues of them into all the Galilee and the demons casting out.
pieces: He went into their synagogues all over Galilee, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} proclaimed the message and threw out demons.

L.39: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, proclaiming in their synagogues throughout all Galilee and casting out the demons.

R.39: Jesus went all over Galilee. He preached in their synagogues and forced demons to leave people.

decisions.choice: he came, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "he was preaching". The meaning is much the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a summary of his work: preaching and casting out demons
decisions.reason: Mark sums up a time of travel in a sentence; preaching and casting out demons go together, as in 3:14-15.

decisions.choice: threw out (B); forced ... to leave (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as in 1:34.

records.source: Καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτὸν λεπρὸς παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ γονυπετῶν λέγων αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.
records.gloss: And comes to him a leper begging him and kneeling and saying to him, If you are willing you are able me to cleanse.
pieces: A man with a serious skin disease came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Falling on his knees, he pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are willing, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have the power to make me clean."

L.40: And a leper comes to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, begging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kneeling, and saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are willing, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able to cleanse me."

R.40: A man with leprosy, a bad skin disease, came to Jesus. He got down on his knees and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want to, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can heal me and make me clean!"

decisions.choice: leper: a person with a skin disease that made him unclean
decisions.reason: The word covered many skin diseases, which the law of Leviticus 13 tells the priests to judge. Not all were what is now called leprosy.

decisions.choice: unclean: he had to live apart from others
decisions.reason: A person with such a disease had to live outside the town and warn others away (Leviticus 13:45-46). Touching him made a person unclean.

decisions.choice: cleanse: heal the disease and make him clean before God's law
decisions.reason: Being cleansed meant the disease was gone and he could rejoin the community and its worship.

decisions.choice: and kneeling, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts do not have these words. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a man with a serious skin disease (B); a man with leprosy, a bad skin disease (R)
decisions.reason: "Leper" now sounds like a label for an outcast, and leprosy today names one disease. Balanced names the condition more broadly; Readable keeps the familiar word and explains it.

records.heading: A man with a skin disease is made clean

records.source: καὶ ὀργισθεὶς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἥψατο καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι·
records.gloss: And having become angry, having stretched out the hand of him he touched and says to him, I am willing, be cleansed.
pieces: Stirred with anger, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and touched him. "I am willing," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told him. "Be made clean!"

L.41: And becoming angry, stretching out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched [him] and says to him, "I am willing; be cleansed."

R.41: Jesus was angry. He put out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and touched the man. He said, "I do want to. Be healed and clean!"

decisions.choice: becoming angry, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts read "moved with compassion". A few, including Codex Bezae and some Old Latin copies, read "becoming angry", which the SBLGNT prints. Scribes were more likely to soften anger into compassion than the reverse, and Mark speaks of Jesus' anger elsewhere (3:5; 10:14). Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: angry: Mark does not say at what
alternatives: angry at the disease and the evil behind it
decisions.reason: Jesus' anger may be at the disease and its power over the man, or at a world that shut him out. Nothing in the story says he is angry with the man, whom he heals at once.

decisions.choice: he touched him: he touched a man the law called unclean
decisions.reason: Touching an unclean person made one unclean (Leviticus 5:3). Here cleanness passes from Jesus to the man instead.

decisions.choice: I am willing: the answer to "if you are willing"
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up the man's own word (1:40).

decisions.choice: touched him (B); touched the man (R)
decisions.reason: Greek can leave out the object; English needs it.

records.source: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἡ λέπρα, καὶ ἐκαθαρίσθη.
records.gloss: And immediately went away from him the leprosy, and he was cleansed.
pieces: In that moment the disease was gone from him, and he was clean.

L.42: And immediately the leprosy went away from him, and he was made clean.

R.42: Right away the skin disease went away, and the man was healed and clean.

decisions.choice: he was cleansed: made clean by God's act through Jesus' word
decisions.reason: The passive verb answers Jesus' command "be cleansed" (1:41).

decisions.choice: immediately: the cure was instant and complete
decisions.reason: The disease left at once, before the priest could examine him.

records.source: καὶ ἐμβριμησάμενος αὐτῷ εὐθὺς ἐξέβαλεν αὐτόν, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὅρα μηδενὶ μηδὲν εἴπῃς, ἀλλὰ ὕπαγε σεαυτὸν δεῖξον τῷ ἱερεῖ καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου ἃ προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: And having sternly charged him immediately he sent away him, \v 44 and says to him, See nothing to no one you say, but go yourself show to the priest and offer for the cleansing of you what commanded Moses, for a testimony to them.
pieces: Jesus gave him a stern warning and sent him away at once.
"Be sure you tell no one about this," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "Instead, go and let the priest examine you. Then offer what Moses required for your cleansing. That will be evidence to them."

L.43: And sternly warning him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} immediately sent him away
L.44: and says to him, "See [that] you say nothing to anyone, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."

R.43: Jesus quickly sent him away with a strong warning.
R.44: He said, "Do not tell anyone about this. Go and show yourself to the priest. Then give the offering that Moses commanded for people who are made clean. That will prove to them that you are clean."

decisions.choice: sternly warning: speaking with deep feeling and force
decisions.reason: The word describes strong emotion, at times a snort of anger (14:5). Here it gives force to the warning that follows.

decisions.choice: sent him away: sent him out at once
decisions.reason: This is the verb of 1:12 and 1:34. It shows urgency, not anger at the man.

decisions.choice: show yourself to the priest: the law of Leviticus 14
decisions.reason: A priest examined a person healed of a skin disease and declared him clean. Then the person offered the sacrifices the law of Moses set out, and could return to the community.

decisions.choice: as a testimony to them: proof to the priests and people that he is clean
decisions.reason: "To them" most likely means the priests and the people. The words can also carry a warning, as in 6:11 and 13:9.

decisions.choice: tell no one: Jesus does not want to be known as a healer only
alternatives: a test of the man's obedience
decisions.reason: Jesus keeps his work quiet, as with the demons (1:34), and the man's report soon stops him entering towns (1:45).

decisions.choice: evidence (B); prove to them that you are clean (R)
decisions.reason: "Testimony" sounds like a speech in English; the word here means proof.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἐξελθὼν ἤρξατο κηρύσσειν πολλὰ καὶ διαφημίζειν τὸν λόγον, ὥστε μηκέτι αὐτὸν δύνασθαι φανερῶς εἰς πόλιν εἰσελθεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἔξω ἐπ’ ἐρήμοις τόποις ἦν· καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν πάντοθεν.
records.gloss: But he having gone out began to proclaim much and to spread abroad the word, so that no longer him to be able openly into city to enter, but outside in solitary places he was; and they were coming to him from everywhere.
pieces: But the man went off and began telling everyone, spreading the news of what had happened, so much that Jesus could not go into any town openly anymore. He kept to deserted places out in the country, and still people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from every direction.

L.45: But he went out and began to proclaim [it] freely and to spread the word abroad, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was no longer able to enter a town openly, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was outside in deserted places; and they kept coming to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from everywhere.

R.45: But the man went away and told many people what had happened. He spread the news everywhere. Because of this, Jesus could not go into a town where people could see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed out in lonely places. But people still came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from everywhere.

decisions.choice: he went out: the man who was healed
decisions.reason: The subject changes to Jesus only in the next clause, "so that he was no longer able". Some read Jesus as the one proclaiming throughout, but the man's disobedience fits 1:44.

decisions.choice: the word: the matter, what had happened
decisions.reason: The word can mean the message (2:2), and Mark may play on it, since the man "proclaims" as John and Jesus do. Here it is the news of his healing.

decisions.choice: so that: the result of the man's talking
alternatives: the reason Jesus avoided towns from the start
decisions.reason: Because of the crowds, Jesus could no longer come into a town openly.

decisions.choice: deserted places: the word for wilderness again
decisions.reason: As in 1:35, Jesus is out where no one lives, and yet people come to him there, as they came to John (1:5).

decisions.choice: the man; Jesus
decisions.reason: Greek moves from one "he" to another. Balanced and Readable name each one.
